name: Shortest GCD Paths
description: You are given three integers $$$n$$$, $$$a$$$, $$$b$$$. Consider a weighted undirected graph with $$$n$$$ vertices, where for every pair of distinct vertices $$$(u, v)$$$ there is an edge with weight: $$$$$$ w(u, v) = \frac{\max(u, v)}{\gcd(u, v)} $$$$$$ Here $$$\gcd(x, y)$$$ denotes the greatest common divisor (GCD) of integers $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$. Find the shortest path from vertex $$$a$$$ to vertex $$$b$$$ in this graph.
input_specification: The only line contains three integers $$$n$$$, $$$a$$$, $$$b$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 10^{9}, 1 \le a, b \le n, a \neq b$$$).
output_specification: Print one integer — the length of the shortest path from vertex $$$a$$$ to vertex $$$b$$$.
approach_summary: Apply Knapsack and Basic Dynamic Programming paradigm under the Dynamic Programming (DP) framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
